result.title: Definitions, Label Names, or Demonstrations? Auditing What Governs LLM Annotation
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to annotate social-science texts, but high accuracy does not establish that they apply researcher-supplied category definitions: predictions may instead reflect prior associations with category labels or labeled demonstrations. We introduce a counterfactual audit that reassigns definitions among output labels, distinguishing adherence to supplied definitions from preservation of a dataset's original mapping. Across three political-text datasets, models rarely follow reassigned definitions, and standard fine-tuning strengthens the original mapping without reliably increasing definition adherence. We then study retrieval-augmented annotation. Retrieving the nearest training examples generally outperforms retrieving examples separately within each category despite using fewer demonstrations. On the two tasks with substantial gains, direct \(k\)-nearest-neighbor classification recovers 74--93\% of the improvement, indicating that neighborhood labels provide much of the predictive signal. Relabeling fixed demonstrations redirects predictions, whereas aligning demonstrations with reassigned definitions substantially increases adherence to the new mapping. Thus, accuracy-improving interventions need not increase codebook adherence; definitions, category labels, demonstrations, retrieval, and training data should be aligned and validated jointly.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出一种反事实审计：把类别定义在输出标签间重新分配，从而区分 LLM 标注时是遵循研究者给定的定义，还是沿用数据集的原有标签映射，并在三个政治文本数据集及检索增强设定下检验定义、标签名与示例各自的作用。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「替换所提供的证据、观察输出是否随之改变」的干预设计可供核查并借鉴到 VLM，用于判断推理答案究竟依赖视觉证据还是语言先验与标签关联，即视觉旁路与证据使用问题。
